discovery_expectations.text: Discovers Truncate uses len() instead of rune count (unicode truncation bug)
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestTruncate_multibyteRuneCountEqualsMaxLen_BUG (line 68) and TestTruncate_midRuneSliceProducesInvalidUTF8_BUG (line 126) explicitly document that Truncate uses len(s) (byte count) at string_utils.go:10 and s[:maxLen] at line 13, which operates on bytes not runes. Summary.md Bug 1 and Bug 3 describe this in detail.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests ExtractInitials with empty string input (index out of range panic)
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestExtractInitials_emptyAndWhitespace (line 336) tests empty string input with expected result ''. The implementation uses strings.Fields which returns no tokens for empty input, so the loop body (p[0]) is never reached — the test passes and confirms the safe path. The BUG tests (lines 366, 396) also note the p[0] byte-access concern. The empty string case is covered in the table at line 339: {"empty string", "", ""}.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests WrapText with zero or negative width
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestWrapText_widthZeroPutsEachWordOnOwnLine (line 488) tests WrapText with width=0. TestWrapText_widthOneAllWordsSingleChar (line 498) tests width=1. Negative width is not explicitly tested as a separate case, but width=0 is covered with an assertion that each word lands on its own line.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests SlugifyText with input containing only special characters
discovery_expectations.evidence: TestSlugifyText_specialCharactersDropped (line 198) includes the table entry {"only special chars", "!@#$%^&*()", ""} at line 205, asserting the result is an empty string.

discovery_expectations.text: Tests all functions with empty string input
discovery_expectations.evidence: Empty string is covered for all five functions: Truncate via TestTruncate_noTruncationWhenStringFitsExactly table entry 'empty string any limit' (line 19); SlugifyText via TestSlugifyText_emptyAndWhitespaceInputs table entry 'empty string' (line 183); CountWords via TestCountWords_tableTests table entry 'empty string' (line 287); ExtractInitials via TestExtractInitials_emptyAndWhitespace table entry 'empty string' (line 339); WrapText via TestWrapText_emptyAndWhitespaceInputsReturnEmpty table entry 'empty string' (line 447).

Each calls t.Skip with a message beginning with 'BUG:'.

quality_expectations.text: Generated tests compile and run without syntax errors — check Go syntax
quality_expectations.evidence: Static analysis confirms correct Go syntax: package declaration 'package stringutils' matches implementation; imports are valid ('strings', 'testing'); all test functions follow the signature func TestXxx(t *testing.T); table-driven tests use correct struct literal and range syntax; t.Errorf, t.Skip, strings.HasPrefix, strings.Split, strings.HasSuffix calls are all valid. No Go toolchain was available to run the compiler, but no syntax errors are detectable through static inspection.

quality_expectations.text: Skipped BUG tests actually fail when unskipped (bug is real, not a false positive)
quality_expectations.evidence: All skipped bugs are verified against the implementation source: (1) Truncate at string_utils.go:10 uses len(s) (byte count) not rune count, and line 13 slices by byte offset — confirmed real for multibyte input. (2) Truncate has no negative maxLen guard — s[:maxLen] with negative index is a real Go runtime panic. (3) ExtractInitials at string_utils.go:44 uses rune(p[0]) byte access — confirmed produces wrong codepoint for multibyte first characters. (4) WrapText at string_utils.go:58 uses len() in the width comparison — confirmed causes premature wrapping for multibyte/emoji input. All bugs are grounded in specific line-level code evidence.
